title: He worked at Princeton, UCL and King's College London before coming home. In 2026, the world's math community gave him its top young-mathematician honour.

sources.text: IISc - Prof Mahesh Kakde wins Ramanujan Prize 2026
ThePrint - From IISc to Cambridge, Mahesh Kakde becomes 5th Indian to win Ramanujan Prize for Mathematics

caption:
He worked at Princeton, UCL and King's College London before coming home. In 2026, the world's math community gave him its top young-mathematician honour.

The $10,000 international honour, announced September 30, 2026, is jointly awarded by the Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics and the International Mathematical Union to a mathematician from a developing country - making Kakde the fifth Indian ever to win it.

His research sits in noncommutative Iwasawa theory - a corner of pure mathematics far from headlines, recognised by one of the field's most selective international prizes.

Kakde's career arc - India to the world's top math departments and back to IISc - is the kind of return migration that strengthens India's research base from the inside.
